recipes.name: Chicken Zucchini Bake
ingredients_raw: 2 cups cooked, shredded chicken breast meat

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Open the cans of crescent rolls, unroll the dough, and place the dough into the bottom of an 11x15-inch baking pan. Do not separate the rolls. Press the edges of the dough up the sides of the pan to make a shallow crust. Spread the honey mustard over the dough.

Place the zucchini and a few tablespoons of water into a saucepan over medium heat, cover, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low, and cook the zucchini until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain and set the zucchini aside. Place the onion in a large skillet with butter over medium heat, and cook and stir until the onion is translucent, 5 to 8 minutes. Stir the cooked zucchini and chicken into the onion, and mix well. Let the mixture heat for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Spread the zucchini mixture in an even layer over the crust.
In a bowl, beat the eggs with salt, black pepper, basil, oregano, and garlic powder; pour the egg mixture over the zucchini. Sprinkle the cheese over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven until the egg mixture is set and the cheese is browned and bubbling, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Zucchini Bake
raw_recipe.description: A baked chicken and zucchini dish, made with cooked chicken breast meat and prepared crescent roll dough, is a tasty, easy meal when you have a lot of zucchini. Honey mustard adds a sweet zing.

video.description: When zucchini is abundant, this seems to be a favorite way to use it! Simple and extremely tasty! If you want it for breakfast -- eliminate the chicken! Add in extra veggies if you want, and you have a wonderful dish to go around!

review.reviewBody: OMG SO SO GOOD!!!! Let me start off by saying I was very skeptical about this recipe. I just put down my fork and yet I want more. This recipe is such a surprise you will be blown away by the flavor.. Love love love this recipe!**Update we made this recipe again for the thousand time, this time we seasoned the chicken with lemon pepper omitted the honey mustard and used just a small amount of ranch dressing in it's place. Everything else we kept the same and it turned out AMAZING! It tastes like our favorite pizza from straw hat pizza the lemon pepper chicken pizza this is how we will be making this recipe from now on it's so delicious

I’m sure this recipe is delicious as is, but I made quite a few changes. I’ve been trying to stay a little healthier, so I don’t have any crescent rolls on hand and decided to omit them completely. I used a rotisserie chicken, which I broke into pieces, removing the skin. I sliced up a whole onion as well as one bunch of green onions, and sliced two large zucchinis into 1/2 lengthwise then into 1/2 circles. I sautéed the white onion first, added the zucchini, added the chicken, then added the green onions. Everything was softened but not overly mushy. I spread all that into a 9x13 Pyrex dish. Then I whisked the eggs together with some buttermilk (could use any type of milk - I just had some that needed to be used up), all of the recommended spices plus a lil more, as well as 2T whole seed dijon mustard (not honey mustard). I poured it on top of the chicken vegetable mixture, making sure it was spread evenly. I then used grated parmesan instead of mozzarella, sprinkling that evenly over the top. I baked for about 25 minutes then popped into the broiler for another 5 minutes or so. It’s pretty good! I would liken it to a crustless quiche kind of thing, best paired with a mixed green salad. You could probably add fresh salsa or tomatoes after. Overall, I would make again, adding more veggies - sautéed mushrooms and spinach would be delicious! Sausage could mix well too. There is a lot of room for improvisation with this dish.

This was a huge hit with my kids. I used several suggestions from other reviewers - Used 1 package of crust and only half of second to fit in the pan, prebaked it about 5 minutes.
 I was worried about dish being too watery. So I spiralized zucchini and yellow squash and sautéed with the onion. I added some minced garlic at the end. It probably does not need 1/4 cup butter. I drained some liquid off. 
I used an extra egg and added some half and half. Seasoned eggs with the salt, pepper, and 1/2 tsp Italian herb mix. 
I would not eliminate the honey Dijon, unless you don't like the flavor in general. It was a significant flavor and a good balance.

This was very good! I made a couple of changes from other reviews. I only had one can of the rolls so used that & a 10x10 pan because it fit in my toaster oven. I let the zucchini drain with a little salt on in for about 20 minutes before cooking it with the onion mixture. I also added some chopped Anaheim pepper to the onions because we love the flavor. I included about 1/2 cup of milk with the eggs. No butter in mine, just some olive oil to cook with the onions. The texture was excellent, not runny or too liquid at all. I also used some cheddar cheese with the motzzarella. Great flavors together.

Surprisingly very good. I did use marinated left over Cornish hen and it added to the taste so if I use chicken next time I will have make sure it is not just plain. Even my son liked it. I only used 1 can of crescent rolls in 13x11 cake pan and baked it at 375 until the casserole was brown on top including the middle. Be sure and do the onions as requested it adds to the taste.

Love this recipe.
 I made the original recipe several times, and have now made a few changes. I prefer to sautee the zucchini with the onion along with some Italian spices.
Being more gluten conscious lately, I substitute the Pillsbury crust for a hash brown crust. I lightly sautee frozen hash browns in some olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then press into a pan. Then, follow the original directions. YUM! Freezes well also.

I scaled this recipe in half and baked in a 9x7-inch dish. I had some Gruyere in the fridge, so used that instead of mozzarella, and steamed the zucchini for 2-1/2 minutes in the microwave. I used a Pillsbury crescent roll dough sheet, and If they’re available at your store, I’d recommend you use them. I steamed the zucchini until not quite tender. This casserole was heading to the oven for 20 minutes, and I didn’t want mushy zucchini. Would do that again, worked perfectly! This is a really mellow casserole, no ingredient really jumps out, simply delicious, and we thoroughly enjoyed it.

I cooked 2 strips of bacon then cooked the onion, zucchini and half a chopped red pepper in the fat. I also beat the eggs with 1/2 + cup of milk. Only used 4 oz cheese. It wasn't too dry. Hubby said it was a bit bready.

I wanted to make this gluten-free, so I substituted a package of cooked brown rice spaghetti for the crescent rolls. It was very good! I sauted the onions and zucchini, and took the advice of using 4 eggs. I also had some cream I wanted to use up, so added 1/2 cup to the egg mixture. Chopped up a fresh tomato, that I also wanted to use up, and sprinkled it on top before the egg mixture was poured on. It was great! Very versatile and substitute-welcome recipe! Thanks!

Yum! I layed the excess dough over the edges and rolled up around the casserole to make a crescent roll crust. Looks as great as it tastes. The honey mustard was a tasty surprise and I used honey Dijon mustard. If you can't find it just use Dijon and add honey to it. This is now one of my top favorite casserole dishes, family thinks so too.

this was delicious! i cut the chicken breast into pieces with salt and pepper and then baked it @425 for 25 mins. I steamed the zuccini and then added the chicken and zuccuni to the onion mix. I only used 1 can of biscuits because that was all i had and just smooshed them into a 9x13 pan and then drizzled honey mustard on top of them. topped with the chicken mix and then when i did the egg mix with the seasonings, i only used 2 eggs (because thats all i had). i also topped it with cheddar cheese instead! i also topped it with a sprinkle of salt! very tasty!!!
awesome!!!
Delicious! We used baked chicken with Italian seasoning. Our puff pastry was also the Hawaiian style which really added to it. Will definitely be making this again!
The taste was OK but won’t be making this particular recipe again. Even after cooking for 45 the crust was still I cooked. The egg took forever to cook. Kind of a soggy mess.
This was really good. I did add mushrooms & drizzled bbq sauce delicious n top. Definitely making this again.
This is so good! I made it exactly how the recipe says. It’s a new dinner staple!
Very good recipe. I made it as the recipe is written. However, it would be very easy to alter to your taste. I will definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing!!!
It was okay. I needed to drain the zucchini for about 20 minutes after cooking. I don’t think I would make it again.

So we ( my wife and I ) made this exactly per the recipe. We did not make any changes. After coming out of the oven, we let it cool a bit. So my family tried this and did not care for it. Everyone thought the same thing that it is missing something. I myself could instantly taste the garlic powder. I did use the honey dejon mustard and could not taste it. I could not taste the others as well; the oregano, basil, salt, and paper. But the garlic powder I could taste very heavily. My wife refuses to make it again. I honestly think that if the chicken was flavored first with a chicken seasoning or an Italian seasoning that it may add more flavor. I had also tried two more pieces one with the Herdez Salsa Verde and the other with the Herdez Salsa Verde and a dollop of daisy ( sour cream ). Eating it this way tasted like enchiladas. Although my wife refuses to make it again, I would try it again, but season the chicken first and chang out the garlic powder for onion powder. And I would tweak it just a little bit for all our tastes. Then I would re-rate this a better star(s).
I used a frozen pie sheel instead of the rolls
